title: SLO Regression Detection and Mitigation Playbook
author: Ravi Patel
body:
Purpose
This playbook describes how Redwood's SRE team detects, classifies, and mitigates SLO regressions across serving, routing, and model-backed features. It is intended for on-call engineers, on-call leads, and service owners.

Scope
- Services: all inference-facing services, routing layers, caching/KV subsystems, and the control plane pieces that affect SLOs (auth, rate-limiting, billing).
- SLO types: latency P50/P95/P99, availability (success rate), request-level correctness checks (synthetic prompt checks), and queueing/backpressure targets.
- Exclusions: long-term quality regressions due to model drift (handled by Applied ML).

Summary of responsibilities
- On-call engineer: triage alerts, execute immediate mitigations, and populate incident record.
- Service owner: coordinate follow-up, approve rollbacks, and lead post-incident review.
- Observability team: review and tune detector thresholds quarterly.

Detection: signals and correlated telemetry
Primary signals (automatic detectors):
1) SLO burn rate alert (default: burn_rate > 10 sustained for 3m) — triggers P1.
2) Sustained P95 latency > configured target + 30% for 5m.
3) Error rate (5xx or model-failure codes) > baseline + 0.5% absolute for 2m.
4) Synthetic probe failures: Canary prompt failure rate > 2% for 10m.
5) Queue depth/backlog increase > 2x typical 95th for 5m.
6) Cross-service spike in client retries or dropped requests.

Secondary signals (recommended correlations):
- Infrastructure: GPU utilization, host OOMs, node reboots.
- Network: inter-region latency spikes, packet loss on egress.
- Config changes / rollouts: deployment events, model variant toggles, routing policy changes.

Example detector implementation (PromQL + comments)
- SLO burn rate:
  sum(rate(error_count[5m])) / sum(rate(success_count[5m]))
  // Adopt per-SLO labels: service, slo_name, region. Create alerts when burn_rate > 10 for 3m.
- Latency regression (P95):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[2m])) by (le, service))
  // Compare to slo_target: if p95 > slo_target*1.3 for 5m -> alert.
- Synthetic probe example (pseudo):
  probe_failures_ratio = probe_failed_total / probe_total

Alerting policy conventions
- Severity mapping: P1 (service impact, immediate mitigation required), P2 (degraded but tolerable, mitigation within 1 hour), P3 (non-critical, follow-up ticket).
- Pager rules: P1 pages SRE on-call and service owner; P2 pages on-call only.
- Auto-silencing: if a P1 is triggered and an active mitigation ticket exists with a documented mitigation strategy, suppress duplicate alerts for 10m.

Triage play (first 10 minutes):
1) Validate alert: open observability dashboard for service, check burn-rate, P95, error-class breakdown.
2) Check recent deploys/rollouts: kubernetes events, CI deploy IDs, model rollout logs (last 30m).
3) Run quick smoke tests from two regions (curl or SDK): record request IDs and latencies.
4) Identify whether issue maps to: serving runtime, model quality, routing/caching, infra (node/GPUs), or external dependencies.
5) Classify incident type: Capacity, Regression, Degradation, Dependency, or Configuration.

Immediate mitigations (choose applicable steps; aim to restore SLO quickly):
A) Capacity-driven regressions
   - Increase target pool size (hot path): trigger autoscale policy override to +30% for 15m.
   - Add capacity: spin up pre-provisioned GPU nodes (runbook CLI: redwood infra capacity scale --service <svc> --delta 4 --reason "SLO burn")
   - Reduce concurrency per worker: temporarily lower max concurrent requests to favor latency.
B) Serving/runtime regressions
   - Toggle to a lower-latency model variant or quantized profile via routing policy. Command: redwood route set-variant --service <svc> --variant <fallback> --rollback-window 30m.
   - Rollback the last runtime change: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<svc> --to-revision=<prev>
C) Model-quality or prompt regressions
   - Cutover synthetic traffic to previous model version; enable canary-only rollback for full traffic after 5m validation.
   - Throttle user-facing traffic by 10–30% using rate-limiters to reduce noise while rollback is validated.
D) Configuration or dependency failures
   - Revert config changes via config-store and redeploy. Keep config-change id in incident notes.
   - Route around the dependency: change to a cached response or local stub if available.

Containment checklist (for on-call to mark in incident record)
- [ ] Primary SLO impact confirmed
- [ ] Mitigation action taken (describe)
- [ ] Traffic reduction / capacity change executed (times & commands)
- [ ] Customer-facing status page updated if impact > 10 minutes
- [ ] Pager rotation and owner notified

Escalation and decision gates
- If burn rate remains > 5 for 30 minutes despite mitigations -> escalate to SRE lead and product on-call.
- If mitigation may cause user-visible degradation (rate-limits, rollbacks), notify customer-success for enterprise customers within 15 minutes.
- Use change freeze exception channel to allow urgent rollbacks outside normal release window.

Recovery and follow-up actions
- Short-term (within 24h): implement resilient routing fallback, increase synthetic probe cadence to 1m, and create follow-up ticket with RCA owner.
- Medium-term (3–14 days): capacity adjustments, permanent routing policy changes, or runtime fixes (kernel or batching modifications) tracked on JIRA.
- Long-term (30–90 days): postmortem with action items, quality/regression guardrails added to model onboarding, and SLO target review.

Runbook: Example commands and snippets
- Check P95 by service (CLI wrapper): redwood obs query "histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[2m])) by (le,service))" --service <svc>
- Scale dedicated pool (example): redwood infra capacity scale --pool redwood-dedicated-pool --add-gpus 4 --ttl 30m --ticket <incident-id>
- Route to fallback variant (example JSON patch):
  { "service": "translate", "route": { "primary": "gptx-3-120b", "fallbacks": ["gptx-3-60b-quantized"] } }

Monitoring hygiene and tuning cadence
- Quarterly review: detector thresholds, burn-rate sensitivity, and synthetic probe coverage.
- Monthly: observe false-positive rate for SLO alerts; aim to keep false-positive rate < 20%.
- After every incident: update playbook steps and detector queries within 5 business days.

Incident review and evidence standards (post-incident)
- Evidence to collect before retro: timeline of alerts, CI/CD deploy IDs, model rollout IDs, sampled request IDs and traces, host-level metrics, and synthetic probe logs.
- Postmortem template: impact summary, detection timeline, root cause analysis (with evidence), action items (owner + due date), and verification criteria.
- Severity-based retention: P1 and P2 incidents -> mandatory 90-day readout; P3 -> optional.

SLO & error-budget policy examples (table)
| SLO name | Target | Burn-rate threshold (P1) | Escalation |
| inference-availability | 99.95% monthly | burn_rate > 8 | SRE + service owner |
| inference-p95-latency | 500ms global | p95 > 650ms for 5m | SRE on-call |
| embedding-success-rate | 99.9% | error delta > 0.2% | SRE + applied-ml |

Retention of artifacts and follow-up verification
- Store incident artifacts in /incidents/<incident-id>/, include dashboards snapshots, trace links, and command history.
- Verification: owner marks action item complete only after associated SLO is observed back to target for a minimum of 72h (unless action specifically limited to a different window).

Ownership and contact matrix (table)
| Area | Primary on-call | Secondary | Pager |
| Serving runtime | runtime-oncall@example.redwood.com | runtime-senior@example.redwood.com | #sre-runtime |
| Model routing | routing-oncall@example.redwood.com | routing-engineer@example.redwood.com | #sre-routing |
| Capacity | capacity-oncall@example.redwood.com | infra-lead@example.redwood.com | #sre-capacity |

Related automation and tooling tasks (actionable items)
- Add a synthetic probe per top 20 customer prompts and ensure per-region coverage.
- Build a quick rollback playbook for common model toggles (CLI + telemetry guardrails).
- Implement an incident CLI wrapper that captures deployment/model IDs automatically when an alert fires.

Appendix: Example Prometheus alert rule (YAML snippet)
- name: SLOBurnRateHigh
  expr: |
    sum(increase(slo_error_count[5m])) / sum(increase(slo_request_count[5m])) > 0.10
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: P1
  annotations:
    summary: "High SLO burn rate for {{ $labels.service }}"
    runbook: "/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/slo-regression-detection-and-mitigation-playbook-2025"

Appendix: Post-incident verification checklist (short)
1) All action items have owners and due dates.
2) Synthetic probes show traffic parity for 72h.
3) SLOs are stable at target for 72h post-fix.
4) Retro draft posted within 5 business days.

Revision history
- 2025-02-14: Created by Ravi Patel (initial playbook).

- 2026-01-12: Clarified burn-rate thresholds and added escalation gates.
